facts.statement: Arthropterygius fossils date from the Kimmeridgian to possibly the Berriasian.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Kimmeridgian–？Berriasian~

facts.statement: The genus Arthropterygius was described by Maxwell in 2010.
facts.quote: authority: Maxwell, 2010

facts.statement: Arthropterygius was found in Canada, Norway, Russia, and Argentina.
facts.quote: Arthropterygius is a widespread genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur which existed in Canada, Norway, Russia, and Argentina from the late Jurassic period and possibly to the earliest Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Arthropterygius lived during the late Jurassic and possibly into the earliest Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Arthropterygius is a widespread genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur which existed in Canada, Norway, Russia, and Argentina from the late Jurassic period and possibly to the earliest Cretaceous.

facts.statement: All species of Arthropterygius measured between 3 and 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Arthropterygius appears to have been a relatively large ichthyosaur, with all species measuring between 3 - 5 m long.

facts.statement: Specimen PMO 222.655 was estimated to be between 3.8 and 4.3 meters long.
facts.quote: The partially preserved specimen PMO 222.655 has been estimated at 3.8 - 4.3 m based on comparisons to the contemporary ophthalmosaurid Undorosaurus.

facts.statement: Arthropterygius had a very short but robust snout relative to its skull length.
facts.quote: It is unusual among ichthyosaurs in having a very short, yet also robust rostrum for its skull length.

facts.statement: The eye socket of Arthropterygius was about 0.34 times the length of the skull.
facts.quote: As a result, the orbit appears very large (about 0.34× the skull length).

facts.statement: Arthropterygius possessed a pineal foramen larger proportionately than any other ophthalmosaurid.
facts.quote: The skull bears a very large pineal foramen, which is larger proportionately than that of any other ophthalmosaurid.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the large pineal foramen in Arthropterygius was an adaptation to high-latitude environments.
facts.quote: This may potentially be an adaptation to the high latitude environment of Arthropterygius, but it is not yet well understood how the size of the pineal eye relates to latitude in ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Arthropterygius had relatively large, robust, conical teeth that were straight or slightly recurved.
facts.quote: The teeth are relatively large, with robust, conical crowns, and are largely straight or slightly recurved.

facts.statement: At least 43 vertebral segments were present in front of the sacrum in Arthropterygius.
facts.quote: the preserved centra suggest that there are at least 43.

facts.statement: The humeral shaft of Arthropterygius was approximately 20% narrower at its midpoint than at its maximum width.
facts.quote: At the midpoint of the humeral shaft, the bone is mildly constricted, being approximately 20% narrower than the maximum width.

facts.statement: The bottom end of the Arthropterygius humerus was larger than the top and bore three articular facets, including one for the ulna forming a 120° angle with the radial facet.
facts.quote: The bottom end of the humerus is larger than the top end; it bears three articular facets, with one for the preaxial accessory element (the smallest of the three), one for the radius (the tallest of the three), and one for the ulna (which forms an angle of 120° with the radial facet).

facts.statement: The top end of the Arthropterygius ilium is 1.5 times wider than the acetabular end, a unique trait for the genus.
facts.quote: Autapomorphically, the top end of the ilium is 1.5 times the width of the acetabular end.

facts.statement: The fused ischiopubis of Arthropterygius is uniquely shorter than the femur among ophthalmosaurids.
facts.quote: Also uniquely among ophthalmosaurids, this fused element is shorter than the femur.

facts.statement: The femur of Arthropterygius has ends of approximately equal width with a slightly narrower middle shaft.
facts.quote: Both ends of the femur of Arthropterygius are approximately the same width, with the middle of the femoral shaft being slightly narrower.

facts.statement: The fossils of Arthropterygius represent the most complete ichthyosaur remains found in the Canadian Arctic.
facts.quote: Its fossils are the most complete of any ichthyosaur in the Canadian Arctic.

facts.statement: A skull and forefin of an ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur were described in 2012 from the Neuquén Basin in Argentina.
facts.quote: In 2012, a skull and forefin discovered of an ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur discovered in the Neuquén Basin of Argentina were described.

facts.statement: The geological outcrops in Svalbard containing Arthropterygius fossils date to the Volgian stage, roughly corresponding to the Tithonian-early Berriasian.
facts.quote: These outcrops likely date to the Volgian (which roughly corresponds to the Tithonian-early Berriasian) based on ammonite biostratigraphy.

facts.statement: In 2019, Zverkov and Prilepskaya revised Arthropterygius, determining that Janusaurus and Palvennia are junior synonyms of the genus.
facts.quote: An extensive revision of Arthropterygius conducted by Zverkov and Prilepskaya in 2019 revealed Janusaurus and Palvennia to be junior synonyms of that genus.

facts.statement: Zverkov and Prilepskaya recognized the taxon "Ichthyosaurus" volgensis from Russia as a new species of Arthropterygius, named A. volgensis.
facts.quote: They also recognize the previously dubious taxon "Ichthyosaurus" volgensis from Syzran in Russia as belonging to a newly recognized species of Arthropterygius, A. volgensis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Janusaurus, Keilhauia, and Palvennia should be treated as synonyms of Arthropterygius, as some studies suggest the evidence does not support this synonymy.
facts.quote: While Zverkov and some others treat Janusaurus, Keilhauia and Palvennia within Arthropterygius, a study on the Jurassic Ichthyosaurs performed by Delsett et al. suggests the synonymy is not supported by the presence evidence.

facts.statement: Maxwell (2010) classified Arthropterygius as the sister taxon to the Argentine ophthalmosaurid Caypullisaurus.
facts.quote: Maxwell 2010 found it to be the sister taxon of Caypullisaurus, an ophthalmosaurid from Argentina.

facts.statement: Many recent cladistic analyses classify Arthropterygius as the basalmost member of the family Ophthalmosauridae.
facts.quote: However, many recent cladistic analyses found it to be the basalmost member of the Ophthalmosauridae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Arthropterygius are found in high-latitude locations across the Northern Hemisphere and one isolated site in Argentina.
facts.quote: Arthropterygius appears to have been a particularly wide-ranging genus, with fossils known from several high latitude localities across the Northern Hemisphere, as well as an isolated specimen from Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of A. chrisorum, A. lundi, and A. hoybergeti come from the Slottsmøya Member of the Agardhfjellet Formation.
facts.quote: The Slottsmøya Member of the Agardhfjellet Formation, from which fossils of A. chrisorum, A. lundi, and A. hoybergeti have been recovered, provides perhaps the best glimpse into the ecosystems and habitats this genus was a part of.

facts.statement: The seafloor at the Slottsmøya Member site was located about 150 meters below the surface and was relatively oxygen-poor.
facts.quote: The seafloor, which was located about 150 m below the surface, seems to have been relatively dysoxic, or oxygen-poor, although it was periodically oxygenated by clastic sediments.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest sea ice was likely present at the Slottsmøya site during winter due to its high latitude and the cool Tithonian climate.
facts.quote: Though direct evidence from Slottsmøya is currently lacking, the high latitude of this site and relatively cool global climate of the Tithonian mean that sea ice was likely present at least in the winter.

facts.statement: The Slottsmøya Member contains fossils of other marine reptiles including Undorosaurus gorodischensis, Nannopterygius borealis, and Brachypterygius sp.
facts.quote: In addition to Arthropterygius, the Slottsmøya Member presents a diverse assemblage of other marine reptiles, including the ichthyosaurs Undorosaurus gorodischensis, Nannopterygius borealis, and a partial skull attributed to Brachypterygius sp.

facts.statement: The Slottsmøya Member includes 21 plesiosaurian specimens, with Pliosaurus funkei likely serving as the apex predator.
facts.quote: Additionally, 21 plesiosaurian specimens are also known from the site, including two belonging to the large pliosaurid Pliosaurus funkei, which would have been the apex predator of the ecosystem, three to Colymbosaurus svalbardensis, one to Djupedalia engeri, one to Ophthalmothule cryostea, and one each to Spitrasaurus wensaasi and S. larseni.

facts.statement: Four species of Arthropterygius (A. chrisorum, A. volgensis, A. lundi, and A. hoybergeti) are found in the Volga region of Russia.
facts.quote: Material belonging to four species of Arthropterygius, A. chrisorum, A. volgensis, A. lundi, and A. hoybergeti, has been reported from the Volga region of Russia, which gives the Volgian stage its name.

facts.statement: The species A. thalassonotus is found in the Vaca Muerta Formation of the Neuquén Basin in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: A. thalassonotus hails from the Vaca Muerta Formation of the Neuquén Basin in Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Arthropterygius chrisorum is the type species of the genus Arthropterygius.
facts.quote: subdivision: Arthropterygius chrisorum Maxwell, 2010 (especie tipo)

facts.statement: Ophthalmosaurus chrisorum is a synonym of Arthropterygius chrisorum.
facts.quote: synonyms: Ophthalmosaurus chrisorum Russel, 1993

facts.statement: Arthropterygius is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur that lived in Canada during the Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Arthropterygius es un género extinto de ictiosaurio que existió en Canadá durante el periodo Jurásico.

facts.statement: Arthropterygius is a new genus for the species previously known as Ophthalmosaurus chrisorum, named in 1993 from fossils found on Melville Island in the Northwest Territories.
facts.quote: Arthropterygius es un nuevo género para la especie antes conocida como Ophthalmosaurus chrisorum, nombrada en 1993 de fósiles hallados en la isla Melville en los Territorios del Noroeste.

facts.statement: Fossils of Arthropterygius are the most complete of any ichthyosaur found in the Canadian Arctic.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles son los más completos de cualquier ictiosaurio en el Ártico canadiense.

facts.statement: A. chrisorum is distinguished from Ophthalmosaurus by features including an articulation between the radius and ulna and a very angled humerus, and an internal carotid artery foramen on the posterior surface of the basisphenoid.
facts.quote: A. chrisorum tiene varias características que lo separan del género Ophthalmosaurus, incluyendo una articulación entre el radio y el cúbito y el húmero muy angulosa y un foramen para la arteria carótida interna (una arteria mayor que abastece de sangre al cerebro) sobre la superficie posterior del basisfenoide.

facts.statement: Arthropterygius lived from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages, between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Tithonian (161.5 to 143.1 million years ago)
